summary: AARNet Engineering Note 001: naming guidelines for the AARNet X.500 Directory Service, recording current or proposed practice at the Australian Academic and Research Network.

plainLanguage.summary: This engineering note explains how AARNet names directory entries in its Australian X.500 service. It follows Standards Australia for the country tree and groups directory servers under a pseudo-organization.

subtitle: Naming rules for entries in the AARNet X.500 directory service.

tldr.problem: AARNet wanted its X.500 directory naming to align with Standards Australia where national and Internet naming guidance differed.
tldr.mechanism: The note describes how to place Australian localities, organizations, directory servers, and residents under the country entry in the directory tree.
tldr.outcome: It records AARNet's proposed or current operational practice and the differences from RFC 1384. It is informational.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 1562 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo documents AARNet directory naming practices from its publication period.

sections.title: Purpose and National Alignment
sections.content:
RFC 1562 is AARNet Engineering Note AEN-001 for administrators of X.500 Directory System Agents. AARNet participates in the global X.500 directory service.

The note says AARNet generally follows Internet documents that supplement X.500, but chooses to align naming with Standards Australia when the guidance conflicts. It records differences from the Internet directory naming guidelines in RFC 1384.
sections.plainLanguage: This note is for AARNet directory administrators. It explains how Australian naming rules affect the directory tree.

sections.title: The Australian Directory Tree
sections.content:
Standards Australia specifies that organizations with nationally recognized names and localities for states and territories may be placed directly under c=AU. The note adds that ADMD and PRMD names are treated like nationally recognized organizations.

The eight states and territories are represented as locality objects using the stateOrProvinceName attribute and standard Australian abbreviations. An organization unique within Australia may go directly beneath the country entry; one unique only within a state or territory goes beneath that state's entry.
sections.plainLanguage: The country entry contains nationally unique organizations and state or territory entries. Organizations whose names are unique only locally are listed under the relevant state or territory.

sections.title: Directory Servers, Organizations, and Residents
sections.content:
To avoid placing many directory-server entries directly under the country node, AARNet creates a pseudo-organization called DMD for Australian DSAs. The note suggests naming DSAs after Australian fauna.

An organization's distinguished name must be its officially registered name and may be at most 64 characters; additional familiar names may help people search. A resident's entry goes below the state of residence and combines the person's common name with a street address.
sections.plainLanguage: Directory servers are grouped under DMD to keep the country entry less cluttered. Organizations use registered names, while residents are listed under their state.
